'''Rachel Hogan''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|OBE}} (born 1976), is a British [[primate]] [[conservation biology|conservationist]], living and working in [[Cameroon]] in West Africa, and director of the charity [[Ape Action Africa]].

Having moved to the Mefou National Park in Cameroon temporarily in 2001, Hogan decided to stay and has been there ever since, becoming director of the charity in 2010. She is well known for her work in the rescue and rehabilitation of gorillas and chimpanzees, as well as fighting the illegal [[bush meat]] trade in West Africa.

==Biography==
Rachel Hogan was born in [[Birmingham]], [[England]] and her interest in animals started during her childhood, when she had toy gorillas instead of dolls.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/england/7686038.stm|title=Gorilla fascination started young|date=24 October 2008|publisher=|via=news.bbc.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.africanconservation.org/content/view/1140/406/|title=African Conservation Foundation - News|access-date=September 11, 2019|archive-date=28 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928061409/http://www.africanconservation.org/content/view/1140/406/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Manager at Mefou National Park ===

In 2003, Hogan was appointed manager of the National Park. During her tenure, she and her team have transformed Mefou into one of the largest, most well known primate conservation charities in Africa.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://theworld.org/stories/2017/03/10/cameroons-gorillas-find-sanctuary|title=Cameroon's gorillas find sanctuary|website=Public Radio International|access-date=September 11, 2019}}</ref>

In October 2008, Hogan was awarded the IFAW Animal Action Award at a ceremony at the House of Lords. The IFAW awards ceremony was hosted by patron Baroness Gale and wildlife TV presenter Shauna Lowry announced the winners.<ref name="bristolzoo.org.uk"/><ref name="zandavisitor.com"/>

Having attracted several celebrities and renowned wildlife photographers to visit the Mefou National Park, Hogan organised a photographic exhibition at the Djeuga Palace Hotel in Yaounde in early October 2010. It was attended by Cameroonian Government Ministers, military heads and representatives from the British, US and Israeli embassies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.facebook.com/media/set/?set=a.443554728575.243368.58336053575|title=Ape Action Africa Photo {{sic|Exh|bition|nolink=y}} Launch - Facebook|website=www.facebook.com}}</ref>

Hogan has also mobilized support for Ape Action Africa through events in Britain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bristol247.com/2011/03/17/bristol-zoo-teams-up-with-womad-for-summer-spectacular|title=Bristol 24/7 - Bristol Zoo teams up with Womad for summer spectacular|website=bristol247.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810071119/http://www.bristol247.com/2011/03/17/bristol-zoo-teams-up-with-womad-for-summer-spectacular/|archive-date=2011-08-10}}</ref>

=== Director of Ape Action Africa ===
On 22 November 2010, the longstanding director of [[Ape Action Africa]], [[Avi Sivan]], was killed in a helicopter crash between Douala and Yaounde in Cameroon.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.4apes.com/news/viewnews.php?id=677&lang=en|title=Ape Alliance and PASA - PASA Mourns Tragic Death of Cameroon Sanctuary Director|website=4apes.com|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005064410/http://www.4apes.com/news/viewnews.php?id=677&lang=en|archive-date=2011-10-05}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.cameroon-today.com/cameroon-helicopter-crash-ex-israel-defense-forces-idf-top-officer-killed/1975/|title=CAMEROON HELICOPTER CRASH: EX- ISRAEL DEFENSE FORCES (IDF) TOP OFFICER KILLED. - Cameroon Today - Breaking News - Daily News Updates|date=22 November 2010|website=cameroon-today.com|access-date=31 May 2011|archive-date=30 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170630035948/http://news.cameroon-today.com/cameroon-helicopter-crash-ex-israel-defense-forces-idf-top-officer-killed/1975/|url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-3988506,00.html|title=Ex-IDF officer killed in Cameroon crash|date=23 November 2010|newspaper=Ynetnews}}</ref> Sivan had long been a driving force within the charity and a close ally of Hogan. Just over a month later, the board of trustees of the charity announced Rachel Hogan as the new Director.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://whogivesamonkeys.com/2011/02/05/new-appointment-for-ape-action-africa/|title=New appointments for Ape Action Africa|date=5 February 2011|website=whogivesamonkeys.com}}</ref> They also appointed Bibila Tafon (Babs) as the new Manager of the Mefou National Park.

One of Hogan's first moves was to bring the administrative offices of the charity back to the Mefou National Park from [[Yaounde]], to improve communications between the conservation efforts and administrative necessities of the charity.

=== Bush meat activism and education ===
Hogan has campaigned against the illegal poaching and selling of rain forest animal species for many years - and particularly the exploitation of chimpanzees and gorillas in this way.

Many of the communities living around Cameroon have hunted primates for meat for centuries, but the recent commercialization of the trade has led to a large increase in the demand for bush meat, a trend that Hogan has been fighting at many levels.

Hogan has introduced a grassroots educational program, in which local charity workers visit communities and schools to teach about bush meat.

Local employment at Ape Action Africa has also helped to spread the message, as well as benefiting the community.

In February 2010, bush meat was discovered on a market in Hogan's hometown, Birmingham and identified as chimpanzee meat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sundaymercury.net/news/midlands-news/2011/02/27/chimp-meat-discovered-on-menu-in-midlands-restaurants-66331-28243001|title=Chimp meat discovered on menu in Midlands restaurants|first=Sunday|last=Mercury|date=27 February 2011|website=sundaymercury.net}}</ref>
